toolchains.note: The host C compiler CMake already uses. C99 is the floor: the public headers use nothing newer, and the gate is what keeps it that way.
The host C++ compiler. A C ABI that a C++ consumer cannot include is only half an ABI, so every header is compiled in both languages.
GCC by name, including C23, which the host compiler may predate.
GCC's C++ driver at the standards CNA itself builds with.
A second front end catches what one compiler's extensions would hide.
Clang's C++ driver, for the same reason.
A Windows target reached by cross-compiling. Headers only: nothing here links or runs a Windows binary, and the matrix says so rather than implying a tested platform.

configurations.note: No window, no GPU. Every route that needs neither is proven here, and every route that does is proven to refuse.

EasyGL's GL ES 3 profile with a real GL context on the private display, in the multi-renderer tree that also compiles SDLGPU, WEBGPU and FNA3D. It replaced the SDL_RENDERER configuration when that renderer was retired on 2026-10-13.
A CPU rasteriser: a third renderer answer for every capability query, and the compiled-out devices half again.

AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer with leak detection on. This is what catches a handle that outlives its owner or an operation nobody released. It runs the CPU rasteriser with the devices half compiled in, which is the one pairing the other three rows leave out: SOFTWARE is therefore exercised in both CNA_DEVICES states.

unsupported.subject: Running a Windows binary
unsupported.note: The cross-compiler proves the headers parse for a Windows target; nothing here links or executes one, so no Windows behaviour is claimed.

unsupported.subject: macOS, as a cell of this matrix
unsupported.note: The matrix records the reference Linux host and its declared configurations, and macOS is not one of them. It was measured separately on Apple silicon (Apple M4 AM4-209..213): every C API test passed in the SOFTWARE and the since-retired SDL_RENDERER configurations there, the dylib exports exactly the cna_* ABI, and CApi_InstalledConsumer builds and runs the installed package, shared and static. docs/c-api/CONSUMING.md has what a macOS consumer needs to know.

unsupported.subject: iOS and Android targets
unsupported.note: No mobile toolchain is a cell of this matrix, so it makes no mobile C ABI claim. iOS builds of CNA itself exist (docs/apple-platforms.md); the C ABI is not exercised on either mobile target here.

unsupported.subject: Web targets, as cells of this matrix
unsupported.note: The WEBGL2 and WEBGPU Emscripten C ABI artifacts are built and exercised separately under Node and in real browsers, as documented in docs/c-api/WASM_ARTIFACT.md. They are not native compatibility configurations, and this matrix does not claim that its complete native smoke-program set runs under either web renderer.

unsupported.subject: C89
unsupported.note: The headers use `//` comments and mixed declarations, so C99 is the floor by design rather than by accident.

unsupported.subject: Renderer identities absent from these configurations
unsupported.note: The configurations run HEADLESS, OPENGLES3 and SOFTWARE. Other public renderer identities share the same C surface, and capability queries are what a caller uses to discover what any active renderer supports.
